newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.
newsitem.headline: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.

text.p: Vacant primary elevator space remained unchanged for the second week in a row as railcar unloads at export ports fell well below target, Canadian Wheat Board said.
Average vacancy in Prairie elevators was 18 percent in the week ended March 23, CWB said.
Weather and equipment failure caused delays in shipping grains and oilseeds to Pacific ports since early January.
The effect has been a severe backlog of vessels on the Pacific coast and more than C$15 million in demurrage fines levied against the CWB.
Twenty-three ships waited to load at Canada's Pacific ports with 11 ships waiting more than 30 days, one as long as 43 days on Friday.

Manitoba elevators had the least space available with 12 percent vacant versus 14 percent the prior week, Saskatchewan was next at 18 percent vacant, up from 17 percent the week before and Alberta had the most space at 22 percent vacant, up from 21 percent the prior week.
Vancouver saw 2,975 railcars unloaded compared to the target of 3,400 hopper cars. The prior week saw 3,121 unloads.
Prince Rupert unloads totalled 1,088 railcars compared to the target of 1,500 hopper cars. Last week saw 1,213 unloads.
Thunder Bay saw 501 railcar unloads compared to the target of 1,150 hopper cars. The prior week saw 621 unloads.
